sections.html:
Homes in this Okaloosa County city cost much less than the national average. A typical owned home is valued at $277,900 for 2020-2024, while the U.S. figure is $332,700.

Newcomers keep arriving. The city had 20,978 residents in 2010 and 27,134 in 2020, and the newest estimate reads 31,193, or 13.8 percent more than the 2020 base. Middle household income is $65,480, so what local buyers can offer is limited.

Crestview stretches across 16.58 square miles. Owners occupy 61.3 percent of homes, households average 2.55 people, and a commute takes 30.4 minutes.

Rent here is a hair under the national $1,413, yet incomes lag, so buyers count every dollar of the monthly payment. If you can show a realistic tax and insurance estimate, negotiations go more smoothly.

Three elected county offices matter. The property appraiser decides what your parcel is worth, the tax collector sends the bill, and the circuit court clerk files your deed. The sheriff and the supervisor of elections hold the other two elected county posts.

Values are set as of January 1, and the appraiser also decides exemption claims. The collector takes care of deferrals, installment plans and certificate sales. At recording, the clerk gathers the deed tax. Phone each one for current forms, hours and fees tied to your parcel.

The Revenue Department's page shows 70 cents for each $100 as the rate Okaloosa uses, and s. 201.02 sets it. Whichever party promises to pay, every party on the document stays liable.

  • Filing starts at $5.00 for the first page, then $4.00 a page, with add-on charges.
  • Each name after the fourth costs another $1.00.
  • The deed needs two witnesses.

Quitclaim deeds are taxable. If a homestead moves between spouses and the only consideration is a mortgage, it may be exempt.

sections.h2: Homestead rules and the next owner's bill
sections.html:
An exemption of up to $50,000 comes off taxable value for a homesteaded Crestview house, with $25,000 of it applying to school taxes. Leave the house, rent it out or sell it, and the exemption is gone.

While you own it, the Save Our Homes cap holds increases to the lesser of 3 percent or CPI. A fast-growing city can push market value past that cap, so the buyer's first bill may be a shock. Property with no homestead is limited to 10 percent a year. Any sale or foreclosure sets just value again the following January 1.

sections.h2: What if there is a tenant, an heir or a lender?
sections.html:
Florida attaches a timetable to each case.

  • Tenants: 3 days after a rent demand, 7 days after a lease violation, 30 days to close a month-to-month arrangement.
  • Estates: a short-form administration is possible at $150,000 or under, and creditors get three months after first notice.
  • Foreclosure: the auction comes 20 to 35 days after judgment, with a 5 percent deposit and 10 days for objections.

A person with no lease at all gets different treatment. The owner can file a sworn complaint with the sheriff, but a false statement exposes the owner to damages of triple the fair market rent.

Okaloosa keeps to the statewide yearly rhythm.

  • January 1: the date values are fixed.
  • March 1: exemption applications close.
  • August: proposed-tax notices are mailed.
  • 25 days after the notice: final day to petition on value.
  • November: bills arrive, and paying that month saves 4 percent, dropping to 1 percent in February.
  • April 1: late.

Your closing agent will split the year's bill with the buyer, so ask how that will be shown on the statement.

Accounts left unpaid go out as certificates by June 1, bought by whoever bids the lowest interest rate. The certificate holder must wait until two years after April 1 of the issue year to apply for a deed, and that application costs $75.

A homestead at a tax deed sale starts bidding at what is owed plus half of the assessed value. The high bidder leaves a nonrefundable deposit, either 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger. A closing that pays off the balance ends the problem far sooner.

sections.h2: Life estate deeds and family transfers
sections.html:
A gift of title to a relative usually counts as an ownership change, unless a narrow exception like a spousal transfer fits. The Revenue Department also treats quitclaim deeds and contracts for deed as taxable.

In 2020 the Department of Revenue issued an advisement about a so-called lady bird deed. On those facts the deed moved no present beneficial interest, and no doc stamp tax applied. Since the answer rested on specific facts, show any such deed to a Florida attorney before counting on it.

• Lender payoff figure, plus a check of the parcel for liens.
  • Homestead status, because any exemption you hold ends at closing.
  • Permit receipts, so a buyer's lender has nothing to stall on. The City of Crestview can pull permit history for your address.
  • Deed logistics: two witnesses, recording with the Okaloosa clerk, and the 70 cents per $100 stamp tax divided as your contract says.
  • A written reply from the tax collector about any deferral or installment plan on your account.

Having this folder ready lets buyers move faster, and it keeps you from scrambling when a title agent calls with a question.

sections.h2: How a direct sale usually unfolds
sections.html:
You describe the house, a buyer makes an offer, and you agree on a closing date. A title company then searches the record, clears any problems and files the deed. Expect to sign a purchase contract, a deed and a settlement statement.

Before you sign anything, read who pays for the title policy and recording, and ask whether the buyer needs any repairs done first. If you have a mortgage, the payoff is taken from your proceeds at the table, and what remains is sent to you after the deed is recorded. Compare more than one offer, and ask each buyer how long they need and how they will pay.

Some Florida veteran exemptions can apply to Crestview owners. They follow the home you live in, so ask the appraiser how yours will be handled when you sell. Many sellers also have children at home, since 28.3 percent of residents are under 18, and they often need the closing date to line up with a new purchase.

Buying again? Get your financing lined up before accepting an offer here. Ask the buyer whether the closing date can bend, and if you need a few extra days in the house afterward, write the arrangement down with an end date.

faqs.q: What does a Crestview home typically cost?
faqs.a: A typical owned home is valued at $277,900 for 2020-2024.
Quickly. The 2025 estimate of 31,193 is 13.8 percent above the 2020 base.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Crestview?
faqs.a: Yes, the deed tax is 70 cents per $100 and all parties are liable. The sales contract decides who pays.

faqs.q: Who can tell me my current property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Okaloosa tax collector bills each November, and the appraiser explains the value behind it.

faqs.q: Can an heir sell a house before probate ends?
faqs.a: Usually not until the personal representative has authority. Ask a probate lawyer or the clerk about the right track, such as summary administration for smaller estates.
